title: Technical Report
text: This technical report documents the methodology and architecture of the NBA Shot Selection Analysis project. It provides an overview of how we collect, clean, and analyze 14 years of NBA shot data to understand trends in three-point shooting adoption and their relationship to team success.

title: Technical Report
text: This technical report documents the methodology and architecture of the NBA Shot Selection Analysis project. It provides an overview of how we collect, clean, and analyze 14 years of NBA shot data to understand trends in three-point shooting adoption and their relationship to team success.

title: Technical Report
text:
1. Data Extraction
We use the NBA Stats API to collect official NBA statistics. The API provides shot-level data directly from the official NBA.com database.
Key endpoints used:

shotchartdetail.ShotChartDetail() – Individual shot attempts with coordinates and outcome
leaguedashteamstats.LeagueDashTeamStats() – Team-level offensive metrics

Data collection parameters:

Time period: 2010–2011 through 2023–2024 (14 seasons)
Teams: All 30 NBA teams
Season type: Regular season only
Context measure: Field goal attempts (FGA)

title: Technical Report
text:
2. Key Findings
Our analysis of 2.8 million shot attempts across 14 seasons reveals three major findings:
Finding 1 — The Three-Point Revolution is Quantifiable League-wide three-point attempt rate nearly doubled over the study period, rising from approximately 20% in 2010–11 to over 39% in 2023–24. This represents the most dramatic strategic shift in NBA history, driven by analytics departments quantifying the efficiency advantage of three-point attempts over mid-range shots.
Finding 2 — Mid-Range Shooting Has Nearly Disappeared Mid-range shots declined sharply as the dominant offensive strategy shifted toward shots at the rim and above-the-break threes. The Houston Rockets most aggressively eliminated mid-range attempts, influencing league-wide trends that followed throughout the study period.
Finding 3 — Three-Point Adoption Correlates With Winning Teams with higher three-point attempt rates show a positive correlation with win percentage, particularly in the recent era (2021–24). This suggests that teams embracing modern shot selection gained a measurable competitive advantage over those that did not adapt.
Teams That Adapted Most The teams showing the largest increase in three-point attempt rate include the Houston Rockets, Milwaukee Bucks, and Golden State Warriors — all of whom experienced significant on-court success during the study period.

title: Technical Report
text:
3. Data Structure

Shot-Level Data
Each shot record includes:

TEAM_NAME – NBA team name
SHOT_ZONE_BASIC – Basic zone classification (e.g., “Above the Break 3”, “Mid-Range”)
SHOT_ZONE_AREA – Detailed zone area
SHOT_DISTANCE – Distance in feet
LOC_X, LOC_Y – Court coordinates
SHOT_ATTEMPTED_FLAG – Whether the shot was attempted
SHOT_MADE_FLAG – Whether the shot was made (1) or missed (0)
SHOT_TYPE – “2PT Field Goal” or “3PT Field Goal”
ACTION_TYPE – Type of action (e.g., layup, jump shot)



Team Metrics Data
Team-season level aggregations:

TEAM_NAME – Team name
season – Season identifier
WINS – Regular season wins
EFG_PCT – Effective field goal percentage
W_PCT – Win percentage

title: Technical Report
text:
4. Cleaning and Standardization
Raw API data undergoes several cleaning steps:

Column standardization – Select and rename relevant columns to lowercase with underscores
Missing coordinate removal – Drop rows where shot coordinates are missing
Backcourt shot removal – Remove heave attempts that are not meaningful for analysis
Three-point flag – Add binary column indicating whether each shot was a three-pointer
Points value – Add column for points scored on each attempt
Era labeling – Classify shots into three eras: Early (2010–14), Mid (2014–19), and Recent (2019–24)
Team name normalization – Standardize historical franchise name changes for consistent tracking:

Charlotte Bobcats → Charlotte Hornets
New Jersey Nets → Brooklyn Nets
New Orleans Hornets → New Orleans Pelicans
LA Clippers → Los Angeles Clippers

title: Technical Report
text:
5. Data Storage
Cleaned shot data is split into four CSV files to stay within GitHub’s 100MB file size limit:

data/shot_data_clean_part1.csv through part4.csv — Shot-level data
data/team_metrics_clean.csv — Team season metrics

The load_shot_data() function automatically reassembles the four part files into a single DataFrame at load time, requiring no manual steps from the user.

title: Technical Report
text:
6. Exploration Workflow
The analysis pipeline consists of:

Data loading – Reassemble and read cleaned CSV files
Aggregation – Group shots by team, season, and zone
Metric calculation – Compute three-point rates, adoption rankings, and correlations
Visualization – Generate court heatmaps, trend lines, and comparative charts

All code is modular and reproducible using Python and standard data science libraries (pandas, matplotlib, seaborn).

title: Technical Report
text:
7. Reproducibility Notes

Python version: 3.11+
Key dependencies: nba_api, pandas, matplotlib, seaborn, streamlit
Data sources: Official NBA Stats API (no paid licenses required)
Runtime: Data collection takes approximately 2 hours for the full 14-season history due to API rate limiting (15 second delay between requests)

To reproduce the full pipeline:
# Step 1 — Collect raw data (run once, takes ~2 hours)
from src.data_collection import get_multiple_seasons_shot_data
from src.data_collection import get_team_season_metrics, save_dataset

seasons = [
    "2010-11", "2011-12", "2012-13", "2013-14", "2014-15",
    "2015-16", "2016-17", "2017-18", "2018-19", "2019-20",
    "2020-21", "2021-22", "2022-23", "2023-24"
]
shots   = get_multiple_seasons_shot_data(seasons)
metrics = get_team_season_metrics(seasons)
save_dataset(shots,   "data/shot_data.csv")
save_dataset(metrics, "data/team_season_metrics.csv")

# Step 2 — Clean the data
from src.data_cleaning import clean_shot_data, clean_team_metrics
from src.data_collection import load_dataset

clean_shots   = clean_shot_data(load_dataset("data/shot_data.csv"))
clean_metrics = clean_team_metrics(load_dataset("data/team_season_metrics.csv"))

# Step 3 — Launch the interactive app
# streamlit run app.py
Note: Pre-cleaned data is included in the repository as four split CSV files (data/shot_data_clean_part1.csv through part4.csv) assembled automatically by load_shot_data(). This allows immediate use without re-running the full collection pipeline.

title: Technical Report
text:
8. Summary
This project demonstrates a complete data science pipeline: from external API collection, through cleaning and standardization, to exploratory analysis and interactive visualization. The methodology is transparent, the code is version-controlled on GitHub, and results are fully reproducible on any machine with Python and internet access. Our analysis quantifies the three-point revolution in the NBA and provides evidence that teams adopting modern shot selection gained a measurable competitive advantage over the 14-season study period.

title: Documentation
text:
Module: src.data_collection
Functions for fetching and saving NBA shot data from the official NBA Stats API.

get_shot_data(team_name, season)
Fetch shot chart data for a single team and season.
Parameters: - team_name (str): Team name, e.g., "Houston Rockets" or "Lakers" - season (str): Season in format YYYY-YY, e.g., "2018-19"
Returns: - DataFrame with shot-level data (coordinates, zones, outcomes)
Example:
from src.data_collection import get_shot_data
df = get_shot_data("Houston Rockets", "2018-19")
print(df.shape)


get_all_teams_shot_data(season, delay=0.6)
Fetch shot data for all 30 NBA teams in a given season.
Parameters: - season (str): Season in format YYYY-YY - delay (float): Seconds to wait between API calls (default: 0.6)
Returns: - Combined DataFrame for all teams
Example:
df = get_all_teams_shot_data("2018-19", delay=0.8)
print(f"Loaded {len(df)} shots")


get_multiple_seasons_shot_data(seasons, delay=0.6)
Fetch shot data across multiple seasons for all teams.
Parameters: - seasons (list): List of seasons, e.g., ["2015-16", "2016-17", "2017-18"] - delay (float): Seconds between API calls
Returns: - Combined DataFrame across all seasons
Example:
seasons = ["2015-16", "2016-17", "2017-18", "2018-19"]
df = get_multiple_seasons_shot_data(seasons)


get_team_season_metrics(season_range)
Fetch team-level offensive metrics for multiple seasons.
Parameters: - season_range (list): List of seasons
Returns: - DataFrame with one row per team per season (wins, offensive rating, etc.)


save_dataset(data, path)
Save a DataFrame to CSV.
Parameters: - data (DataFrame): Data to save - path (str): File path, e.g., "data/shot_data.csv"
Note: Parent directories are created automatically if they don’t exist.


load_dataset(path)
Load a CSV file into a DataFrame.
Parameters: - path (str): File path
Returns: - Loaded DataFrame

title: Documentation
text:
Module: src.data_cleaning
Functions for cleaning and preprocessing raw API data.

clean_shot_data(df)
Clean raw shot data: standardize columns, classify zones, label eras.
Parameters: - df (DataFrame): Raw shot data from API
Returns: - Cleaned DataFrame with standardized columns


clean_team_metrics(df)
Clean raw team metrics data.
Parameters: - df (DataFrame): Raw metrics data
Returns: - Cleaned DataFrame

title: Documentation
text:
Module: src.analysis
Functions for statistical and exploratory analysis.

three_point_rate_by_season(shots)
Calculate league-wide three-point rate (3PA / total FGA) by season.
Parameters: - shots (DataFrame): Cleaned shot data
Returns: - Series with three-point rate indexed by season


rank_teams_by_three_point_adoption(shots)
Rank teams by their overall three-point adoption rate.
Parameters: - shots (DataFrame): Cleaned shot data
Returns: - DataFrame with teams ranked by 3P rate (highest to lowest)


biggest_zone_shifts(shots)
Identify which shot zones have changed most in usage over time.
Parameters: - shots (DataFrame): Cleaned shot data
Returns: - DataFrame showing zone usage shifts


correlate_three_pt_rate_with_wins(shots, metrics)
Correlate team three-point rate with win percentage.
Parameters: - shots (DataFrame): Cleaned shot data - metrics (DataFrame): Cleaned team metrics
Returns: - DataFrame with correlation analysis results

title: Documentation
text:
Module: src.visualization
Functions for creating interactive and static visualizations.

plot_court_heatmap(shots, team, season)
Generate a court heatmap for a specific team and season.
Parameters: - shots (DataFrame): Shot data - team (str): Team name - season (str): Season
Returns: - Matplotlib figure


plot_three_point_trend(shots)
Plot league-wide three-point trend over time.
Parameters: - shots (DataFrame): Shot data
Returns: - Matplotlib figure


plot_zone_distribution_over_time(shots)
Stacked area chart showing zone usage changes over time.
Parameters: - shots (DataFrame): Shot data
Returns: - Matplotlib figure


plot_three_pt_vs_wins(corr_df)
Scatter plot correlating three-point rate with win percentage.
Parameters: - corr_df (DataFrame): Correlation data from correlate_three_pt_rate_with_wins()
Returns: - Matplotlib figure

text:
Complete Example — End to End Walkthrough
Here is a full example that loads the data, runs analysis, and produces a visualization:
from src.data_collection import load_shot_data, load_team_metrics
from src.analysis import (
    three_point_rate_by_season,
    biggest_zone_shifts,
    rank_teams_by_three_point_adoption,
    correlate_three_pt_rate_with_wins
)
from src.visualization import (
    plot_three_point_trend,
    plot_zone_shift_bar,
    plot_top_three_point_adopters
)
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Step 1 — Load data
shots   = load_shot_data()
metrics = load_team_metrics()

# Step 2 — League wide three point trend
trend = three_point_rate_by_season(shots)
print(trend)

# Step 3 — Which zones changed most
shifts = biggest_zone_shifts(shots)
print(shifts)

# Step 4 — Which teams adopted three point shooting most
rankings = rank_teams_by_three_point_adoption(shots)
print(rankings.head(10))

# Step 5 — Does three point rate correlate with winning
corr_df = correlate_three_pt_rate_with_wins(shots, metrics)

# Step 6 — Visualize
fig = plot_three_point_trend(shots)
plt.show()

fig = plot_zone_shift_bar(shots)
